Serve the explorer with plumber2

Source: R/serve.R
grafts_api.Rd

grafts_api() adds an explorer to a plumber2 api, for deploying it (with Docker or Posit Connect, say) or mounting it beside other routes. It adds the routes {path}api/spec, {path}api/series and {path}api/health (for load balancers and containers), and the app's page at {path}, which {path} without its trailing slash redirects to. Responses are cached privately and revalidated with an ETag, so a redeployed dataset is seen at once. grafts_serve() runs an explorer on its own server, for scripts and containers. Printing an explorer from grafts() in the console runs grafts_serve(), blocking the console like a Shiny app until it is stopped.

Usage

grafts_api(api, explorer, path = "/", max_ids = 1000)

grafts_serve(
  explorer,
  port = serve_port(),
  host = serve_host(),
  launch = FALSE,
  block = TRUE
)

Arguments

api

A plumber2 api, such as from plumber2::api().

explorer

An explorer from grafts(), which takes the data, forecasts and options.

path

Where the explorer is mounted on api. Mount several explorers at different paths, such as "/tourism/" and "/retail/".

max_ids

The most series that one request to api/series may ask for. The app asks for up to 200 at a time.

port, host

Where the app is served, by default port 8000 on this machine only. Set GRAFTS_PORT (or PORT) and GRAFTS_HOST, or the options grafts.port and grafts.host, to change the defaults without editing code. Use host = "0.0.0.0" to accept connections from other machines, such as from a container. The app has no sign-in, so put anything private behind an authenticating proxy.

launch

Open the app, in the IDE's viewer where there is one, else in a browser.

block

Block the R session while serving, like a Shiny app. When FALSE, stop the app with plumber2::api_stop() on the returned api.

Value

grafts_api() returns api with the explorer added. grafts_serve() returns its plumber2 api, invisibly.

Details

The data stays in R, and the app is sent each series when it is drawn, so data of any size can be explored.

Examples

if (FALSE) {
# A plumber2 file (plumber.R), for Posit Connect or plumber2::api("plumber.R")
#* @plumber
function(api) {
  data <- readRDS("tourism_agg.rds")
  grafts_api(api, grafts(data))
}

# Several datasets on one api, at /tourism/ and /retail/
plumber2::api() |>
  grafts_api(grafts(tourism_agg), path = "/tourism/") |>
  grafts_api(grafts(retail_agg, forecasts = retail_fc), path = "/retail/") |>
  plumber2::api_run()

# In Docker, from the command line
# Rscript -e 'readRDS("tourism_agg.rds") |> grafts::grafts() |>
#   grafts::grafts_serve(host = "0.0.0.0")'
}
